title: What are the chances for personalised treatment with antidepressants? Detection of patient-by-treatment interaction with a variance ratio meta-analysis

claims.statement: The variance of treatment outcome in antidepressant arms is not larger than in placebo arms (VR = 1.01, 95% CI 0.99 to 1.02, 169 trials, 51,396 patients), so there is no or only very small heterogeneity of individual treatment effect.
claims.scope: Short-term placebo-controlled RCTs of 21 antidepressants in unipolar major depression, restricted to the 169 trials reporting pre-post change scores; drawn from Cipriani et al. (2018).

quantities.name: variability_ratio_antidepressants_reproduced
quantities.source: maria 2026, p02 on the p01 reconstruction; DerSimonian-Laird with Knapp-Hartung, as in their script

our_assessment.why: Reproduced from the public upstream data to three matching integers (169 / 32,650 / 18,746) and four matching statistics (VR, CVR, Q for both, r(M,SD) for both arms). The residual difference in the third decimal is explained: they collapsed dose arms by hand and then drugs in the script, while p01 collapses all antidepressant arms in one pass, and averaging SDs is not associative under regrouping. The claim about VR is correct. What VR then LICENSES about heterogeneity is c4 and c5.

claims.statement: The coefficient-of-variation ratio is 0.82 (95% CI 0.80 to 0.84), i.e. the increase of variance with increasing pre-post difference is weaker in antidepressant than in placebo arms; the authors state there is no immediately plausible explanation for this.
claims.scope: Same 169 trials. Reported as a second finding alongside the VR result and repeated for every drug class.

quantities.name: lncvr_minus_lnvr_max_abs_deviation_from_log_mean_ratio
quantities.source: maria 2026, p02 section 2 -- machine epsilon over all 169 trials

quantities.name: mean_change_ratio_drug_over_placebo_n_weighted
quantities.source: maria 2026, p02 -- n-weighted mean symptom reduction, drug arms over placebo arms

our_assessment.why: It is not a fact about variance. Both statistics carry the identical Nakagawa small-sample correction, which cancels, so per trial lnCVR_i - lnVR_i = ln(m_PL,i / m_AD,i) EXACTLY -- measured max absolute deviation 2.8e-16 across all 169 trials. CVR is VR divided by the ratio of mean symptom reductions and contains no further information. The drug reduces symptoms more than placebo in 159 of 169 trials; on HAMD17 the reduction is 10.99 vs 9.11 points, ratio 1.207, reciprocal 0.829. Their own Table 1 gives VR/CVR = 1.2317 against an n-weighted mean-change ratio of 1.2286, and the identity predicts every subgroup row including the tricyclic outlier (CVR/VR 0.613 vs mean ratio 0.603). The 'no immediately plausible explanation' is the treatment effect. Their code carries the tell: 'for the calculations of CVR, it was necessary to use the absolute values of the pre-post differences' -- a coefficient of variation requires a mean on a ratio scale, and a pre-post change has an arbitrary zero and either sign. FURTHER, 2026-09-06 (see c10): the sign of the result flips with the reporting convention. Their own supplementary table 1 runs the identical analysis on the 84 endpoint-score trials and gets CVR = 1.15, above 1, while VR stays at 0.98.

claims.statement: The switch from VR to CVR is justified because 'the pre-post differences were significantly associated with their SD' (r(M,SD) = 0.55 in drug arms, 0.52 in placebo arms).
claims.scope: One sentence in Statistical analysis, and the r(M,SD) columns of Table 1.

quantities.name: mean_sd_correlation_within_scale_pooled_drug
quantities.source: maria 2026, p04C; Fisher-z pooled over HAMD17/21/24 and MADRS with n-3 weights

quantities.name: within_trial_between_arm_mean_sd_correlation
quantities.source: maria 2026, p04C -- r(ln(m_AD/m_PL), ln(SD_AD/SD_PL)), the correlation that would actually license a CV normalisation

our_assessment.why: Two independent failures. (1) The corpus mixes HAMD17 (k=71), HAMD21 (52), MADRS (24), HAMD24 (12) and four more scales with different ranges, so trials on longer scales have both larger means and larger SDs for reasons unrelated to the drug. Within scale the correlation is +0.045, +0.311, -0.136, +0.421; pooled +0.135. 75% of the cited correlation is between-scale mixing. (2) An ACROSS-TRIAL correlation cannot license a WITHIN-TRIAL, BETWEEN-ARM division. The relevant statistic is r(ln mean ratio, ln SD ratio) = +0.110, p = 0.154, not significant.

claims.statement: MARIA 2026, NEW: the additive-versus-multiplicative choice is a continuous parameter lambda (SD proportional to mean^lambda), it is estimable from aggregate data, and on this corpus lambda = 0.098 [-0.024, 0.241] -- so lnVR's assumption of 0 is inside the interval, lnCVR's assumption of 1 is far outside, and the published CVR applies 10.2 times the correction the data support.
claims.scope: 169 trials. lambda estimated by regressing lnVR on ln(m_AD/m_PL) and rescaling the slope against the same regression run on simulated worlds with lambda = 0 and lambda = 1 by construction. Interval from 4000 trial-level bootstrap resamples.

quantities.name: lnvr_regression_slope_null_lambda0
quantities.source: maria 2026, p08 -- simulated world with additive homogeneity true by construction

quantities.name: lnvr_regression_slope_null_lambda1
quantities.source: maria 2026, p08 -- multiplicative homogeneity true by construction; note the estimator's own scale is 0.515, not 1

quantities.name: variability_ratio_at_estimated_lambda
quantities.source: maria 2026, p08 -- exp(lnVR - lambda*mean ln mean-ratio), against 1.006 at lambda=0 and 0.782 at lambda=1

our_assessment.why: The raw regression slope is NOT lambda -- the same estimator returns +0.0020 and +0.5170 on worlds where lambda is 0 and 1, so its scale is 0.515 and an uncalibrated slope would understate lambda by half. Calibrating against both anchors is what makes the number readable. Robustness: p07 reran the additive null with a bounded generator (a change score cannot exceed the patient's own baseline, and the floor compresses the SD of whichever arm improves more), which moved the additive null to -0.046 while the multiplicative null stayed at +0.524; the observed slope sits close to additive under either generator. Third independent corpus on which this adjudication comes back additive.

claims.statement: MARIA 2026, NEW: pooling a difference of two sample variances by inverse-variance weighting is biased, because the weight is a function of the same random quantities as the numerator, and the bias does not vanish -- it takes the sign of the arm-size asymmetry. On this corpus the naive estimator returns +0.514 points^2 from a world with D = 0 by construction, with 90.2% coverage of a nominal 95% interval.
claims.scope: General to any meta-analysis of a difference of variances; measured here on the 169-trial antidepressant corpus with its real arm sizes and SDs, 500 simulated corpora per cell.

quantities.name: d_estimator_bias_naive_weight_null_world
quantities.ci: 500 simulated corpora; true D = 0 by construction

quantities.name: d_estimator_coverage_naive_weight_null_world
quantities.source: maria 2026, p05 -- realised coverage of a nominal 0.95 interval

quantities.name: d_estimator_bias_equal_arm_sizes
quantities.source: maria 2026, p05 prediction P1 -- forcing n1 = n2 shrinks the bias ninefold

quantities.name: d_estimator_bias_arms_swapped
quantities.source: maria 2026, p05 prediction P2 -- making the placebo arm the larger one reverses the sign

quantities.name: d_estimator_bias_pooled_variance_weight
quantities.source: maria 2026, p05 prediction P3 -- the fix

our_assessment.why: Three falsifiable predictions of the proposed mechanism were stated before running and all three held: equal arm sizes shrink the bias from +0.585 to +0.064; swapping the arms reverses it to -0.567; a weight built from the across-arm pooled variance (which does not contain the difference) removes it, -0.003 with 96.6% coverage. Re-verified at D = +5 and D = -5 (bias -0.070 and +0.125, coverage 96.6% and 95.0%). A common-scale weight also works (bias +0.054) but is less efficient, SD 1.119 against 0.787. The mechanism is the same shape as the coupling artifact in mccutcheon2022: a quantity on both sides of its own estimator.

claims.statement: MARIA 2026, NEW: the identified quantity D = sigma_AT^2 - sigma_PL^2 on the HAMD17 subset is +0.444 [-1.748, +2.637] HAMD points^2 (k = 71, I2 = 0%), which at rho = 0 bounds sigma_TE at 1.62 points -- 0.86 times the 1.88-point mean drug-placebo effect -- and at rho = -0.32 permits 5.45 points.
claims.scope: HAMD17 trials only (the largest single-scale subset, 13,132 drug and 8,147 placebo patients), corrected pooled-variance weight, Paule-Mandel. D carries units and must not be pooled across measurement scales.

quantities.name: sigma_te_upper_bound_at_rho_zero_hamd17
quantities.source: maria 2026, p06 -- from the upper confidence limit of D

our_assessment.why: Accepted as an estimate of D on HAMD17 with the corrected estimator of c5. NOT accepted as a statement about sigma_TE, which is not identified by a parallel-group design (senn2016) and moves by a factor of eight over the rho values this literature has used. The scale restriction is not fastidiousness: the unit-mixed pool over all 169 trials gives +1.188 [-0.477, +2.854], so mixing units moves the answer by more than any difference between the arms does.

claims.statement: Their Figure 1 -- a simulation grid asking how many 'benefiters' of what size are compatible with the observed VR -- is, at rho = 0, the single inequality p(1-p)delta^2 <= D_upper, and it reproduces their own reading of the figure.
claims.scope: HAMD17 subset, two-point mixture of individual treatment effects, rho = 0 assumed exactly as their figure assumes it.

quantities.name: max_benefiter_effect_at_10_percent_rho0
quantities.source: maria 2026, p06 -- sqrt(2.637/(0.1*0.9)); their figure's own reading is 6 points at p = 10%

our_assessment.why: Two independent routes to the same number -- their simulation grid over benefiter definitions gives 'about 6 points at 10%', the closed form gives 5.41 -- which is worth more than either alone because the agreement does not depend on their simulation's parameter choices. The closed form additionally makes the rho = 0 assumption a visible knob: the same bound is 18.17 points at rho = -0.32, so their conclusion that 'the scope for personalised treatment seems to be limited' is carried by an independence assumption they never state.

claims.statement: Their rule for collapsing several antidepressant arms into one -- the unweighted mean of the arm SDs -- is a downward-biased estimator of the combined arm SD, applied to 84 of 169 trials, always on the drug side.
claims.scope: The 84 multi-arm trials. Compared against correct finite-mixture pooling, which adds the between-arm mean spread.

quantities.name: median_sd_deflation_from_mean_of_sds
quantities.source: maria 2026, p03 -- their SD over the correct mixture SD; smaller in 50 of 84 trials, worst case 0.9230

quantities.name: variability_ratio_with_correct_mixture_pooling
quantities.source: maria 2026, p03 -- against 1.0060 [0.9929, 1.0192] under their rule

our_assessment.why: The criticism is correct in direction and immaterial in size, and it is recorded because I expected it to matter and it did not. Averaging SDs is downward-biased twice over (Jensen, plus the omission of the between-arm mean spread) and it is one-sided here because the placebo side is always a single arm. But dose arms of one drug have nearly identical means, so the between-arm term is near zero: the pooled VR moves 1.0060 -> 1.0077, well inside its own interval. Anyone re-deriving this objection should stop at the measurement, not at the argument.

claims.statement: The abstract reports 163 trials; Table 1, the drug/placebo arm totals, and an independent reconstruction from the upstream data all give 169, with the same 51,396 patients.
claims.scope: Bookkeeping. 32,650 + 18,746 = 51,396, the abstract's own patient count.

our_assessment.why: Nothing downstream depends on it -- every analysis in the paper uses the 169 -- but it is recorded because a k quoted from an abstract is how a wrong denominator enters a later synthesis, and the abstract is the part that gets quoted.

claims.statement: MARIA 2026, NEW: the sign of the CVR result is set by the reporting convention, not by the data. In the same paper, on the same drugs, CVR is 0.82 on the 169 trials that reported a pre-post CHANGE and 1.15 on the 84 that reported an ENDPOINT score -- it crosses 1 -- while VR is stable at 1.01 and 0.98. For tricyclics the two values are 0.65 and 1.37, a factor of 2.1.
claims.scope: Their Table 1 (change scores) against their online supplementary table 1 (endpoint scores). Both subsets rebuilt from upstream and reproduced exactly: 84 trials, 10,879 drug and 7,346 placebo patients, VR 0.9803 against their 0.98 and CVR 1.1494 against their 1.15.

quantities.name: cv_ratio_antidepressants_endpoint_subset
quantities.source: their online supplementary table 1; reproduced by maria 2026 p09 as 1.1494 [1.1146, 1.1853]

quantities.name: variability_ratio_antidepressants_endpoint_subset
quantities.source: their online supplementary table 1; reproduced as 0.9803 [0.9634, 0.9975]

quantities.name: cv_ratio_tricyclics_endpoint_subset
quantities.source: their online supplementary table 1 -- same drug class, same statistic, ratio of the two values 2.1

quantities.name: endpoint_score_ratio_placebo_over_drug
quantities.source: maria 2026, p09 -- n-weighted endpoint scores 15.86 placebo vs 13.51 drug; the identity requires CVR/VR to equal this, observed 1.173

quantities.name: trials_where_drug_arm_has_the_smaller_endpoint_mean
quantities.source: maria 2026, p09 -- the sign flip that carries the whole result

our_assessment.why: PREDICTED BEFORE LOOKING, and the prediction is recorded at the top of p09 with the supplement's actual numbers pasted in underneath. From lnCVR - lnVR = ln(m_PL/m_AD): on change scores the drug arm's mean is the LARGER one (it improves more), so CVR < VR; on endpoint scores the drug arm's mean is the SMALLER one (fewer symptoms left), so CVR > VR. The subgroup ordering was predicted too and holds -- tricyclics, with the largest drug-placebo gap in this dataset, are the most extreme in BOTH directions. Reproduced to four significant figures on both subsets from an independent rebuild. The authors interpret the 0.82 substantively and say it has no plausible explanation; the 1.15, which says the opposite, is in a supplement and is not discussed.

relations.why: Independent corpus, independent authors, same conclusion: the variability ratio of antidepressant trials is indistinguishable from 1. Munkholm draws on a different antidepressant meta-analysis; this one on Cipriani et al. 2018.

McCutcheon et al. argue a VR near 1 is compatible with large sigma_TE once rho is negative, and estimate rho = -0.32. Ploderl & Hengartner read VR near 1 as evidence against heterogeneity, which requires rho = 0. Neither states its rho assumption in the abstract. They cannot both be right and no aggregate dataset can decide between them.
relations.asymmetric_note: The disagreement is entirely about an unmeasured parameter, not about any measured quantity: both reproduce, and my p06 shows the same D supports either reading (sigma_TE <= 1.62 at rho = 0, <= 5.45 at rho = -0.32).

relations.why: Both read VR near 1 as absence of heterogeneity of treatment effect, which is only valid at rho = 0, and neither says so. They do not cite each other's assumption because neither names it.

Senn shows a parallel-group design identifies only the between-treatment component and that patient-by-treatment interaction requires within-patient replication. This paper cites that argument correctly in its Introduction -- one of the few in the area that does -- and then draws a conclusion about personalisation anyway.
The additive-versus-multiplicative adjudication with a simulated null slope was developed there; this record extends it from a binary verdict to a continuous parameter lambda with an interval.

The D value of -0.384 [-1.636, +0.868] carried in that record and in the area file was computed with the naive inverse-variance weight now shown biased (c5). It must be recomputed with the pooled-variance weight before being compared with anything.
relations.asymmetric_note: The direction of the bias depends on that corpus's own arm-size asymmetry, which has not been checked, so the old number is not simply too high -- it is unknown until recomputed. Not marked refuted, marked pending recomputation.

open_questions: Recompute D on the Munkholm corpus with the corrected pooled-variance weight. Until then the two D values are not comparable and the -0.384 must not be quoted against the +0.444 here.
Four psychiatric variability meta-analyses still have no D: antipsychotics (Winkelbeiner 2019), brain stimulation, PTSD psychotherapy, depression psychotherapy.

Does lambda differ across drug classes? Tricyclic trials have the largest mean-change ratio and would be the place to look, but k = 3 in my class assignment (theirs was 11 because they counted a trial in every class it contained).

ANSWERED 2026-09-06 by p09 and now claim c10: the endpoint subset gives CVR = 1.15, not because CVR is legitimate there but because the mean ratio inverts. An endpoint score does have a meaningful zero, so a CV is computable on it -- but a CV RATIO between arms still just carries the mean ratio, and the mean ratio is the treatment effect. CVR is not rescued by a better scale; it is the wrong object for a two-arm comparison whatever the scale.
